cells.sectionSub: Transmembrane potential and thermal response computed via Schwan equation. Drag the Field Intensity slider to explore the selectivity window.

healthy.label: Healthy Hepatocyte
healthy.description: Epithelial hepatocyte (R = 10 µm). Lower radius and thicker membrane yield higher Schwan threshold, preserved across the electroporation window targeting larger carcinoma cells.

target.label: Adenocarcinoma Cell
target.description: Carcinoma cell (R = 15 µm). Larger radius and higher membrane permittivity produce elevated transmembrane potential under identical field conditions, enabling size-selective disruption.

paramTips.radius: Cell radius R [µm] Vm scales linearly with R in the Schwan equation. Larger cells reach higher Vm under identical fields, which is the geometric basis of selective disruption.
paramTips.membraneThickness: Membrane thickness d [nm] Sets capacitance: Cm = ε_r × ε₀ / d. Thinner membranes in cancer cells raise Cm and τ, shifting the corner frequency fc downward. Typical lipid bilayer: 4-8 nm.
paramTips.dielectricConstant: Effective membrane permittivity ε_r Relative permittivity of the lipid bilayer. Determines Cm together with d. Higher values reflect altered phospholipid and cholesterol composition. Typical range: 4-10.
paramTips.conductivity: Cytoplasm conductivity σ_i [S/m] Affects the Schwan time constant τ and corner frequency fc. Higher σ_i gives shorter τ and higher fc, compressing the selective window. Typical cytoplasm: 0.3-1.0 S/m.
paramTips.thresholdVoltage: Electroporation threshold Vth [V] Transmembrane potential above which irreversible pore formation is initiated. Disruption ratio is DR = Vm / Vth. Literature range: 0.5-2.0 V.
paramTips.resonantFreqGHz: Capsid resonance frequency [GHz] Fundamental acoustic resonance of the cell wall or viral capsid, set by shell geometry and the cytoplasm speed of sound. Bacteria: 0.3-2 GHz; viruses: 5-20 GHz.
paramTips.capsidQ: Acoustic quality factor Q Sets the sharpness of the resonance peak: half-power bandwidth = f_res / Q. Bacteria: Q ≈ 3-4 (peptidoglycan viscous damping). Protein-capsid viruses: Q ≈ 25-30.

cells.paramsToggleTip: Cell Parameters Edit biophysical properties that drive the Schwan equation calculation in real time. Changes immediately update Vm, selectivity, and the frequency response chart.
cells.paramsToggleTipAcoustic: Cell Parameters Edit acoustic and structural properties that drive the capsid resonance model in real time. Changes immediately update disruption ratio and the frequency response chart.
cells.derivedTip: Derived biophysical parameters Computed in real time from the editable values above. Cm = ε_r × ε₀ / d Membrane specific capacitance [mF/m²] τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i) / (2σ_e·σ_i) Schwan time constant (Kotnik & Miklavcic 2000) Sets the frequency roll-off fc = 1/(2πτ) Characteristic frequency, Vm drops −3 dB here Below fc: quasi-DC regime, Vm at maximum
cells.derivedTipAcoustic: Acoustic resonance constants Computed from the capsid model parameters. τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i) / (2σ_e·σ_i) Schwan time constant (electrical coupling) fc = 1/(2πτ) Schwan corner frequency (electrical roll-off) BW = f_res / Q Half-power bandwidth of the acoustic resonance peak Narrower BW: higher frequency selectivity
cells.resetBtnTip: Reset to Preset Defaults Restores all parameters to the original values for this preset. Useful after editing to explore changes.

cells.tipBlebbing: Membrane Blebs The small circular protrusions visible on the cell surface in the animation. What causes them: the transmembrane electric field generates electrostatic pressure (Maxwell stress) on the lipid bilayer. Where that pressure exceeds the local cortical actin anchoring force, the membrane detaches from the cytoskeleton and inflates as a rounded bleb. Below 85% DR (approaching and rev-EP): blebs cycle in size as transient electroporation pores open and reseal. Osmotic water influx through open pores inflates each bleb; pore resealing reverses the pressure and the bleb retracts. The cell can recover if the field is reduced promptly. Above 85% DR (lysis armed): blebs enlarge without retracting, indicating irreversible cytoskeletal uncoupling. Lysis is imminent at this stage. Ref: Teissie & Rols 1993; Rols & Teissie 1998

targetMetrics.tipElysis: Lysis Field E_lysis Minimum field strength [V/cm] required to lyse this cell at the current frequency, waveform, and pulse width. Rises above quasi-DC as frequency exceeds f_c (membrane cannot fully charge). The selectivity window sits between E_lysis(target) and E_lysis(healthy).
targetMetrics.tipTi: Selectivity Index (TI) TI = DR_target / DR_healthy = ratio of target disruption to healthy disruption at identical field and frequency. TI > 1.5: good selectivity window. TI > 2: strong selectivity. TI < 1: healthy cell more affected than target.
targetMetrics.tipFc: Characteristic Frequency f_c f_c = 1 / (2π τ) where τ = R · Cm · (2σ_e + σ_i) / (2σ_e · σ_i). Below f_c the membrane charges fully (quasi-DC regime, maximum Vm). Above f_c, Vm rolls off at -20 dB/decade. Operating below f_c maximises selectivity for mammalian targets.

slider.title: Field Control
slider.thermalVaporizing: VAPORIZING: T > 100°C · SAR model invalid above boiling point
slider.tipSnapFcH:
Snap frequency to healthy cell corner frequency fc(H) = {fc}
At fc: Vm drops to 1/√2 of quasi-DC peak. Useful for selective τ measurement.
slider.tipSnapFcT:
Snap frequency to target cell corner frequency fc(T) = {fc}
At fc: Vm drops to 1/√2 of quasi-DC peak. Useful for selective target disruption studies.
slider.tipSnapQuasiDC:
Quasi-DC preset: f = fc(T)/20 (ωτ << 1, membrane fully charges each pulse), field at 50% lysis threshold, pulsed 0.01% duty cycle, 100 µs pulses.
Operates in the DC-limit where Vm is maximal and selectivity is determined by size ratio R_T/R_H. Low duty cycle keeps SAR-driven heating below 3°C rise. Use this to characterise the DC-limit selectivity window.
slider.tipSnapSelective:
Selective IRE preset: optimal frequency for maximum selectivity, field at 85% target lysis threshold, pulsed 0.01% duty cycle, 100 µs pulses.
Target DR reaches 85% (lysis armed); lysis fires after N x t_p/dc (~10 s). Low duty cycle limits SAR heating to <8°C so lysis is electroporation-driven, not thermal.
slider.tipSnapNsEP:
Nanosecond pulsed electric field (nsPEF): 1 MHz, supralytic field (200% lysis threshold), 10 ns pulses at 0.001% duty cycle.
Targets intracellular organelles via incomplete membrane charging (pulse << τ). Minimal thermal effect.
slider.tipSnapThermal:
Mild thermal preset: optimal frequency, field at 25% lysis threshold, pulsed 0.1% duty cycle, 100 µs pulses.
Sub-lytic field keeps DR around 25%. SAR accumulation at 0.1% duty cycle drives T_ss to ~40-44°C for hyperthermic sensitisation and biomodulation. Both effects are present simultaneously.
slider.lysisNSub: N × (t_p / dc) = total protocol time above threshold
slider.doubleShellSub: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006) · bandpass nuclear Vm · f_peak ≈ 0.7-2 MHz
slider.tipHfire: H-FIRE: High-Frequency Irreversible Electroporation Bipolar square-wave pulse pairs at carrier frequency >100 kHz. The membrane's RC circuit partially charges on the positive half-pulse, then partially discharges on the negative half-pulse. Net charge per unit peak field is lower than monopolar pulsed, so a higher peak field is needed to reach the same disruption ratio. Key physics differences vs monopolar pulsed: Effective lysis threshold: ×1.75 higher (1.5-2× lit. range) Waveform factor wf = 1.0 (peak field, same as pulsed) SAR heating per unit field: identical to pulsed (wf=1.0) Ref: Arena et al. (2011) Biomed Eng Online; Sano et al. (2015) Sci Rep Set pulse width to the full burst duration, not a single half-cycle.
slider.acousticModeNote: Acoustic resonance mode. Waveform, duty cycle, and pulse width do not apply. Disruption is driven by capsid resonance at f_res, not membrane charging.
slider.tipMinPulse: Minimum pulse width, 3τ rule Full membrane charging requires t_p ≥ 3τ (≥95% plateau). Green: full charging · Amber: partial (τ - 3τ) · Red: sub-threshold (<τ) τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i)/(2σ_e·σ_i) [Kotnik & Miklavcic 2000]

regime.tipElectrolytic: Electrolytic Regime (<300 MHz) Below the Maxwell relaxation frequency of saline (~365 MHz, σ=1.5 S/m, ε_r=74 at 37°C), the medium behaves as a conductor and direct-contact electrodes work well. Hardware: electroporation cuvette · pulse generator · direct wire connection DC impedance model (Z = d/σA) is valid in this regime. Ref: Foster & Schwan (1989) CRC Crit. Rev. Biomed. Eng.
regime.tipNearfieldRf: Near-field RF Regime (300 MHz-1 GHz) Above ~365 MHz the medium transitions from conductor to lossy dielectric. Direct electrodes still work for short path lengths, but EM penetration depth (~32-48 mm in saline, static model) starts to limit sample access. Hardware: coaxial RF probe · impedance-matched coaxial cable · 50 Ω system DC impedance model is approximate, use transmission-line or FEM for accuracy. Ref: Gabriel et al. (1996) Phys. Med. Biol. 41:2271
regime.tipMicrowave: Microwave Regime (>1 GHz) EM penetration depth in saline: ~32 mm (static σ model; real depth shorter above 1 GHz due to Debye relaxation of water). DC electrode coupling is ineffective; only the surface of the sample is accessible. Hardware: rectangular waveguide · resonant cavity · horn antenna Field uniformity is a major challenge. Cuvette geometry sets up standing waves. GHz frequencies are required for acoustic capsid resonance (bacteria/virus). Ref: Gabriel et al. (1996); Tsen et al. (2007) J. Biol. Phys.

slider.electrodePolarizationWarn: Electrode polarization risk: f < 50 kHz. Displayed Vm and DR may be overestimated.
slider.ghzHighFieldWarn: Hardware not feasible: > 1 GHz + > 100 V/cm is physically inaccessible (EM penetration depth limited; Debye relaxation reduces field access in saline above 1 GHz).
slider.ghzHighFieldTip: GHz + High Field: Hardware Inaccessible Delivering >100 V/cm at frequencies above 1 GHz is not achievable with current RF electroporation equipment: EM penetration depth (exact lossy-dielectric model, static σ): 1 GHz → ~32 mm · 10 GHz → ~32 mm (static model; real depth shorter due to Debye relaxation of water). A 4 mm electroporation cuvette attenuates the field substantially at GHz frequencies. The displayed E field does NOT reach the cells at high field + high frequency. The acoustic resonance model used here (Tsen et al. 2007) was demonstrated using pulsed laser stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS), NOT RF electric fields. There is no published demonstration of RF-driven acoustic capsid resonance at the field strengths and frequencies shown here. This parameter combination is physically speculative. Ref: Tsen et al. (2007) J. Biol. Phys. 33:25; Gabriel et al. (1996) Phys. Med. Biol. 41:2271.
slider.electrodePolarizationTip: Electrode Polarization Warning (f < 50 kHz) At low frequencies, the electrode-electrolyte double layer (Cdl ≈ 10-50 µF/cm²) forms a capacitive impedance that absorbs a significant fraction of the applied voltage before it reaches the cells. The simulation assumes all voltage drops across the cell suspension (V = E·d), which overestimates the delivered field and therefore overestimates Vm, DR, and lysis probability. Magnitude: at 1 kHz in saline with typical platinum electrodes, up to 50-80% of applied voltage may be lost to electrode polarization. At 10 kHz: 10-30% loss. At 50 kHz+: negligible (< 3%). To mitigate: use reversible Ag/AgCl electrodes · keep f > 50 kHz · use 4-electrode (tetrapolar) measurement to decouple field and sensing electrodes. Ref: Foster & Schwan (1989) CRC Crit. Rev. Biomed. Eng.; Schwan H.P. (1966) Adv. Biol. Med. Phys. 5:147.

resonance.speculativeBannerTitle: SPECULATIVE MODEL: No experimental RF validation
resonance.speculativeBannerDetail: The Dykeman & Sankey (2010) acoustic resonance model was validated on non-enveloped icosahedral protein capsids (TMV, CCMV). Enveloped viruses (influenza, SARS-CoV-2) have fluid lipid bilayers with no defined elastic modulus or mechanical resonance Q. GHz RF fields also face severe EM field penetration limits in aqueous media at high frequencies (Debye relaxation of water above 1 GHz). These parameters are theoretical extrapolations.
resonance.chartNote: Disruption ratio = (E / E_thr) × L(f, f_res, Q)
resonance.noteBody: Acoustic/mechanical capsid & cell-wall disruption. f_res ≈ v_protein/(2R): viral capsids ~10-12 GHz, bacterial walls ~0.5-1.5 GHz. Mammalian cells (R ≈ 10 µm) have no GHz resonance, frequency-selective disruption. Ref: Tsen et al. (2007); Dykeman & Sankey (2010)
resonance.noResonance: No resonance parameters for this cell
resonance.tipFieldFormula: Disruption ratio = (E / E_threshold) × L(f, f_res, Q)
resonance.tipTargetBadgeNote: ≥100% at resonance → capsid/cell-wall disruption threshold exceeded
resonance.tipHealthyBadgeBody:
Mammalian cells lack rigid-shell resonance, Schwan Vm → 0 at GHz (ωτ ≫ 1).
At f_res(target) in GHz, healthy cell disruption ≈ 0.

drChart.title: Disruption Ratio: f-Domain
drChart.tipTitle: Disruption Ratio vs Frequency Shows DR(f) = Vm(f) / Vthreshold × PEF for both cells. Green region: selectivity window, target DR ≥ 85% while healthy DR < 50%. Dashed amber line = reversible EP boundary (50%). Dashed red line = lysis threshold (85%).
drChart.sectionTip: DR(f) = Vm·PEF / Vm_thr, Amber dashed = Rev-EP 50% · Red dashed = Lysis 85% · Green fill = selectivity window (target ≥ 85%, healthy < 50%)
drChart.zoomTip: Toggle Y-axis scale. Zoom: fits axis to current data range (min 20%). Full: always shows 0-110% with both threshold lines visible.
drChart.disclaimerLowField: Both cells are below 5% DR across all frequencies. Increase the field intensity to see meaningful disruption curves.
drChart.disclaimerBacteriaVirus: Bacteria and virus targets cannot be disrupted at IRE field strengths. These cell types require acoustic resonance protocols (GHz). Switch to Resonance mode.

ai.consentGateBody: Enabling outcome logging allows the AI optimizer to learn from your experiment results. Only protocol parameters and outcome ratings are stored — no identifiable sample data.

ai.rateOutcomePrompt: How successful was this protocol? (1 = failed, 5 = excellent)
ai.tipOptimizeBtn: AI Protocol Optimizer Uses XGBoost trained on your rated experiment outcomes to suggest optimal protocol parameters. The frontend pre-computes all Schwan physics (τ, fc, selectivity). The Python service adds ML-predicted outcome quality beyond the physics baseline. Requires at least 20 rated outcomes to activate ML. Uses the physics baseline until then.
ai.tipApplyBtn: Apply AI Suggestion Applies the suggested frequency, field intensity, duty cycle, pulse width, and waveform to the sliders. Your current settings will be overwritten.

ai.tipPhysicsBaseline: Physics Baseline No ML model trained yet (fewer than 20 rated outcomes). This suggestion is derived purely from the Schwan equation: optimal selectivity frequency and lysis-threshold field for the current cell pair.
ai.retrainNoData: Not enough rated outcomes to retrain
ai.lowConfidenceWarning: Confidence is low ({conf}). Rate more outcomes to improve ML accuracy.
ai.tipTrainingSamples: Training sample count The XGBoost model activates after 20 rated outcomes. Each star-rating you submit in the experiment log adds one training sample. The model confidence score grows from 0.50 (physics baseline) towards 0.90 as more samples are collected.
ai.tipRetrainBtn: Retrain Model Triggers the Python XGBoost service to retrain on all rated outcomes in the SQLite database. Do this after collecting a batch of new ratings to refresh the model's recommendations. Requires the Python AI service to be running.
ai.tabExpandTip: AI Protocol Optimizer Click to open the ML-assisted protocol recommendation panel. Rate your experiment outcomes to train the XGBoost model.

signIn.tipSchwan: Schwan EP Model Computes transmembrane voltage Vm(f) using the Schwan equation for spherical cells. Peak Vm of 1.5 V is achievable at DC or sub-fc frequencies for typical mammalian cells.
signIn.tipResonance: Acoustic Resonance Models mechanical capsid disruption at the cell's structural resonant frequency f_res. fc at 2.4 MHz is the characteristic corner frequency for the simulated cell geometry.
signIn.tipAI: AI Optimizer XGBoost-based model trained on protocol sweep data to recommend pulse parameters. Predicts selectivity ratio and lysis fraction given cell pair and field settings.
signIn.tipSelectivity: Selectivity and DEP Selectivity ratio (TI) measures how preferentially the target cell lyses over the reference cell. A TI of 3.2x means the target reaches lysis threshold at 3.2x lower field than the reference.
signIn.tipWorkspaces: Multi-lab Workspaces Organization-level workspaces let multiple researchers share cell libraries, protocols, and reports. Session state is isolated per user; workspace assets are shared across the team.
